messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging: ELB 502/5xx surge in us-west-2a - aggregated 5xx rate 23% over last 5m. Impact: ~12% of customer requests. Pager duty: oncall-robin.
robin: I'm on it, looking at ELB health and targetgroups first.
robin: aws elb describe-target-health --target-group-arn arn:aws:... -> multiple targets in us-west-2a show Unhealthy (502/504).
ryan: seeing elevated ENI Rx drop counters in us-west-2a from our VPC flow logs, possible egress blackhole?
maria: confirmed increased packet drops on eni-eni path to internet gatewa y in us-west-2a, flows show SYN timeouts.
jaspreet: Route53 healthchecks for service-api-usw2a started failing ~22:03 UTC, TTL 60s, lots of failover chatter.
robin: customers reporting API latency and some timeouts. Impacting read-heavy routes and embedders.
pagerduty: Escalation to SRE oncall (ryan) due to networking component.
ryan: taking over for network-level analysis, handoff timeline: 1745559500 -> I'm the active owner.
robin: handing off remaining app-level triage to maria.
maria: rolling deploys paused, will drain targets in 2a that report unhealthy. Command: aws elbv2 deregister-targets --target-group-arn arn:... --targets Id=i-0abc123 --region us-west-2
robin: good. Also enabling ALB cross-zone load balancing and reducing connection draining TTL to 10s for quick failover.
netops-bot: Runbook step 3: check VPC route tables and NATGW health in AZ a.
ryan: NAT gateway in us-west-2a shows high active connections and some 502 responses; creating temp route to force egress via us-west-2b NATGW to validate.
jaspreet: performing Route53 failover: set weighted routing to shift 70% traffic to us-west-2b, 30% to 2a, TTL 30. Patch command snippet pasted.
robin: FYI customers on long-lived websockets may still see drops until connections rotate; posting on status page now.
olivia: drafting status update: "We are experiencing elevated errors in us-west-2a affecting API requests. Mitigation in progress; routing being shifted to other AZs. No data loss reported."
robin: status update posted to status.redwood.ai with impacts and note about temporary rate limiting for some endpoints. :thumbsup:
ryan: after forcing egress via 2b NATGW, packet drops drop to baseline. Network team confirms possible ENI driver issue in a subset of hosts in us-west-2a. Opening case with AWS.
jaspreet: adjusted Route53 healthcheck window to be more tolerant while we mitigate to avoid oscillation.
maria: drained and marked ~6 targets unhealthy in TG-apisvc-usw2a, shift is holding. Error rates down from 23% -> 4% in 15m.
robin: good improvement. Next steps: keep weighted routing in place until AWS confirms host-level remediation OR until we can repro and patch.
ryan: AWS support case opened: case-id 1234567890. Provided pcap snippets and ENI counters. They are assigning networking team.
netops-bot: Suggested temporary mitigation: scale up cross-AZ capacity and enable NLB fallback in front of ELB for critical endpoints.
jaspreet: NLB fallback applied for embed endpoints. Preliminary tests show stable connections.
olivia: status update #2 posted: "We have shifted traffic away from affected AZ; error rates significantly reduced. AWS engaged."
robin: note for postmortem: include timings for when Route53 weight changed, TG deregisters, NATGW route forces, and AWS case open.
maria: collecting logs and sample traces for regression testing. Will pin a reproducible set.
ryan: adding notes to the incident doc and starting on-call handoff to jaspreet at 1745560800 UTC.
robin: handing back to ry an for AWS case follow-up; I'll monitor customer comms.
jaspreet: taking over for 1h to watch for recurrence. If error rate rises above 8% alert me.
incident-bot: Reminder: Please run post-incident checklist within 48h: RCA, timeline, followups.
olivia: creating a customer-facing summary draft for account teams to send to affected customers.
ryan: AWS responded: they see 'ENI TX ring timeout' on subset of hosts; they will attempt host reset in us-west-2a. ETA 45m.
maria: scheduling canary traffic back after AWS hosts reset and observed stable metrics for 10m.
robin: thank you all. I'll file an incident postmortem template and assign owners for followups (route53 TTL review, NATGW capacity policy, LB fallback runbook).
jaspreet: quick note: remember to update runbook with step to lower Route53 TTL before weighted change to speed fallback for future events.
olivia: posted incident update to internal #customer-impact doc with list of affected tenant IDs and mitigation notes.
incident-bot: Incident status: mitigated -> partial, monitoring. Last update 1745561200.
robin: closing active paging. If anything spikes we can reopen. Great job team. :clap:
